tool_input.description: Confirm the virtualenv exists and show make version

tool_input.command: make -j4 check MAKE='make -f Makefile -f scratch-fail.mk'; echo "exit=$?"
tool_input.description: Prove check stops after a simulated test failure, under -j
Confirm only Makefile and CLAUDE.md changed and the scratch file is gone

result:
Done. `make check` is added and verified. Nothing is committed; git status and diff needed approval, so the changes sit in the working tree on `evals/first-suite`.

**What changed**

- `Makefile`: new phony `check` target with one recipe line per step, calling `$(MAKE) build`, then `test`, then `lint`. Separate recipe lines guarantee the order and stop at the first non-zero exit even under `-j`, which a plain prerequisite list would not. A comment in the Makefile says why.
- `CLAUDE.md`: a `Check:` line in Commands describing healthy and failing output, and a short mention in Verifying your work.

**Verification**

```
$ make build
.venv/bin/python -m compileall -q app && echo "Build succeeded"
Build succeeded

$ make test
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q
........................................................................ [ 48%]
........................................................................ [ 97%]
....                                                                     [100%]
148 passed in 1.26s

$ make lint
.venv/bin/python -m pyflakes app tests ops
```

`make check` ran all three in order with the same output. I also proved the stop-at-first-failure behaviour by overriding `MAKE` with a temporary makefile whose `test` target exits 1, run under `-j4`:

```
make -f Makefile -f scratch-fail.mk build
Build succeeded
make -f Makefile -f scratch-fail.mk test
simulated test failure
make[1]: *** [test] Error 1
make: *** [check] Error 2
```

Lint never ran and make exited 2. The scratch makefile was deleted afterwards and the tree contains only the two edited files.
